known.text: Current cycle: C115
19th St Oakland ridership up 5,324 vs C114 | 8 stations + 10 corridors on the record

19th St Oakland moved up the most this cycle — mild; base: ledger; game day (Downtown); events in Downtown, Lake Merritt, Temescal, KONO; Baylight District — Final Council Vote: construction-active; crowded platforms (city transit congestion 0.12); 14 transit workers on the roster, 7 citizens who lived a transit line.
Day type this cycle: ordinary weekday — no citywide cut. A station that moved more than the citywide rule names its own reason on its row.

The week on the line — every cause on the record this cycle, once: mild; game day (Downtown, Jack London); events in Downtown, Lake Merritt; Baylight District — Final Council Vote: construction-active; crowded platforms (city transit congestion 0.12); game day (Downtown); events in Downtown, Lake Merritt, Temescal, KONO; events in Lake Merritt, Chinatown; events in East Oakland ×2; Fruitvale Transit Hub Phase II — Visioning: design-phase; game day (Jack London); events in Temescal; events in Pie
Weather this cycle: mild, 55°F (5 cycles of clear)

Game on the sports feed this cycle: Oaks at KONO — The Oaks put the Orlando Magic away in the first quarter and made it three straight, Oaks 125 - Magic 109, in front of a 94% crowd at home. Oakland scored 41 in the opening quarter to lead 41-27, went up 73-52 at the half and 101-76 after three, and the Magic only got it respectable by winning a garbage-time fourth 33-24. Adash Stanley led with 24 points, 8 assists and zero turnovers, hitting 6 of 12 from three. AJ Dybantsa bounced back from his

Game on the sports feed this cycle: Oaks at San Antonio — The Oaks went into a sold-out Philadelphia, lost a 14-point lead, and won it back with the best fourth quarter of their young season, Oaks 120 - 76ers 106. Oakland opened 31-17, but the 76ers poured in 36 in the second to cut it to 56-53 at the half and won the third 29-24 to lead 82-80 going into the fourth. Then the Oaks scored 40 and held Philadelphia to 24, turning a two-point deficit into a 14-point win. AJ Dybantsa led with 25 on 10
Eleanor Rivera — BART Station Manager — BART Oakland Division
Calendar: Y3C11, Spring, holiday=none
